marking_points.point: Buffer overflows occur when there is no proper bound checking, allowing buffer content to overspill into adjacent upper stack areas so that an attacker can overwrite the return address.

accepted.question: State six distinct malware attack techniques or propagation methods used to compromise computer systems, drawing on historical examples and executable infection strategies.

marking_points.point: Remote execution exploits were used for network propagation, as demonstrated by the Morris worm leveraging a debugging feature of sendmail to penetrate thousands of computers.
marking_points.quote: Used a debugging feature of sendmail (remote execution)

marking_points.point: For COM executable files, malware propagates by appending its virus body directly to the end of a legitimate host program.
marking_points.quote: Append a virus body to a program

marking_points.point: COM file infection involves replacing the original program entry point with a jump instruction that redirects execution to the virus body first.
marking_points.quote: Replace a program entry point with a jump to a virus body

marking_points.point: For EXE executable files, the attack technique involves overwriting the program header so that the entry point switches to the virus code upon execution.
marking_points.quote: Over write a program header to switch the entry point to a virus

marking_points.point: Self-replication is a foundational propagation technique where programs copy themselves within shared memory environments to increase their survival chances against competing processes.
marking_points.quote: To increase their survival chances, programs can replicate themselves

accepted.question: Describe the Samy worm as a malware case study, explaining how it exploited Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) to propagate and compromise user profiles on a social networking platform.

marking_points.quote: Inject Javascript into a user proﬁle using document.body.innerHTML

marking_points.point: It retrieved the list of a user's heroes by performing a GET request on the target user's profile.

marking_points.point: The worm added its creator as a friend by executing an XML-HTTP request on the addFriends page.
marking_points.quote: Add Samy as a ﬁeld by performing XML-HTTP on the addFriends page

marking_points.point: Any visitor to an infected profile would have their own profile infected with the Javascript and their friends list modified.
marking_points.quote: Any user who visits an infected user's page will gets proﬁle infected with Javascript and his friends list infected with Samy

marking_points.point: The attack achieved massive scale, eventually infecting approximately one million MySpace profiles.
marking_points.quote: Eventually about 1,000,000 MySpace proﬁles were infected.

marking_points.point: The underlying vulnerability exploited by such worms is that any web application returning unfiltered user input enables arbitrary script execution.
marking_points.quote: Any web application that returns user input without ﬁltering is a potential XSS vulnerability!

marking_points.point: Single Sign-On solutions aim to reduce the need for users to memorize multiple passwords across systems.

marking_points.point: During Kerberos user login, the hash value of the entered password becomes the secret key of the client or user.

marking_points.point: A core Kerberos design criterion ensures security against eavesdropping by preventing any password transmission in clear text.

accepted.question: Explain five key aspects of how a Trusted Platform Module (TPM) and the chain of trust work together to establish a trusted computing environment.

marking_points.point: The TPM is defined as a tamper-resistant hardware module mounted in a platform that is responsible for measurement, protected storage, integrity reporting, and policy enforcement.
marking_points.quote: Trusted Platform Module (TPM): a tamper-resistant hardware module mounted in a platform.

marking_points.point: The core idea of the Trusted Computing architecture is that each stage measures and validates the next one during the boot process.
marking_points.quote: Each stage measures and validates the next one

marking_points.point: The measurements taken during the chain of trust process are stored into Platform Configuration Registers located on the TPM.
marking_points.quote: Measurements go into Platform Configuration Registers (PCRs) on the TPM

marking_points.point: The chain of trust begins with the hardware TPM and then proceeds through software components including the RTM, TPM Software Stack, BIOS, and kernel.
marking_points.quote: The chain starts with the hardware TPM, then software: RTM,TPM Software Stack, BIOS, kernel

marking_points.point: A Root of Trust for Measurement is a component trusted to reliably measure and report what software executes at the start of platform boot.
marking_points.quote: Root of Trust for Measurement: the component that can be trusted to reliably measure and report to the Root of Trust for Reporting what software executes at the start of platform boot

questions.question: Discuss six specific obligations that a computing professional must uphold under the ACM Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct to ensure responsible practice in computer security.

marking_points.point: A computing professional must contribute to society and human well-being, acknowledging that all people are stakeholders in computing.
marking_points.quote: Contribute to society and to human well-being, acknowledging that all people are stakeholders in computing.

marking_points.point: A computing professional is obligated to avoid harm in their work.
marking_points.quote: Avoid harm.

marking_points.point: A computing professional must respect privacy as part of ethical conduct.
marking_points.quote: Respect privacy.

marking_points.point: A computing professional should strive to achieve high quality in both the processes and products of professional work.
marking_points.quote: Strive to achieve high quality in both the processes and products of professional work.

marking_points.point: A computing professional must give comprehensive and thorough evaluations of computer systems and their impacts, including analysis of possible risks.
marking_points.quote:
Give comprehensive and thorough evaluations of                                                    computer systems and
their impacts, including analysis of possible risks.

marking_points.point: A computing professional should design and implement systems that are robustly and usably secure.
marking_points.quote: Design and implement systems that are robustly and usably secure.

questions.question: Explain six distinct Windows security mechanisms and features, covering how the operating system manages subjects, access control, directory services, system configuration, historical milestones, and the risks introduced by complexity.

marking_points.point: Windows subjects are processes and threads whose security credentials are stored in a token that provides principal/subject mapping.
marking_points.quote: Security credentials for a subject are stored in a token. Tokens provide a principal/subject mapping and may contain additional security attributes.

marking_points.point: Discretionary Access Control (DACS) enables fine-grained access control of heterogeneous entities within Windows itself as well as applications.
marking_points.quote: DACS enable ﬁne-grained access control of heterogeneous entities in Windows itself as well as applications.

marking_points.point: Active Directory is an LDAP-like directory service introduced in Windows 2000 used for organizing users, groups, security credentials, and policies.
marking_points.quote: Active directory introduced in Windows 2000 is an LDAP-like directory service for organization of system resources:

marking_points.point: The Windows Registry is a hierarchical database containing critical system information, including security-related hives such as the SAM database and security logs.
marking_points.quote: A hierarchical database containing critical system information

marking_points.point: Historical security milestones include Windows Vista introducing no admin-by-default, a firewall, and Data Execution Prevention (DEP).
marking_points.quote: Vista (2007): no “admin-by-default”, ﬁrewall, DEP

marking_points.point: The complexity of Windows security mechanisms can be its enemy because misconfiguration and implementation bugs may lead to severe security incidents.
marking_points.quote: The complexity of Windows security mechanisms is also its enemy: misconﬁguration as well as implementation bugs may lead to severe security incidents.

questions.question: Explain the fundamental mechanism of a substitution cipher and identify the cryptographic principle it embodies.

marking_points.point: In a substitution cipher, plain-text letters are replaced with other letters to produce the cipher-text.
marking_points.quote: In substitution ciphers, we replace the plain-text letters with other letters

marking_points.point: This replacement technique corresponds to Shannon's principle of confusion.
marking_points.quote: Corresponds to Shannon’s principle                                          of confusion

questions.question: Describe six characteristics of access control structures, specifically focusing on the access control matrix (ACM), access control lists (ACL), and capability-based approaches.

marking_points.point: Access control structures are mechanisms for implementing access policies, including the access control matrix (ACM), capabilities (C-List), and access control lists (ACL).
marking_points.quote:
Access control structures are mechanisms for implementing access policies:
access control matrix (ACM)
Capabilities (C-List)
access control lists (ACL)

marking_points.point: The access control matrix (ACM) serves as a basic control structure that offers clarity of definition and is easy to verify.
marking_points.quote:
ACM is a basic control structure.
Advantages:
clarity of deﬁnition
easy to verify

marking_points.point: An ACL provides an object-centered description of access rights, making it relatively easy to manage using abstractions.
marking_points.quote: ACL is an object-centered description of access rights:

marking_points.point: A disadvantage of the ACL structure is that it provides a poor overview of access rights per subject and makes revocation difficult.
marking_points.quote:
Disadvantages:
poor overview of access rights per subject
difﬁculty of revocation
difﬁculty of sharing

marking_points.point: Requirements for access control structures include an ability to express control policies, verifiability of correctness, scalability, and manageability.
marking_points.quote:
Requirements for access control structures:
an ability to express control policies
veriﬁability of correctness.
scalability and manageability

marking_points.point: In practical implementations such as Windows, a DACL in a security descriptor is structured as a list of Access Control Entries (ACE).
marking_points.quote: DACL in a security descriptor is a list of Access Control Entries (ACE)

questions.question: State six distinct malware attack techniques or propagation methods used to compromise computer systems, drawing on historical examples and executable infection strategies.

marking_points.point: Boot sector infection was used as a propagation method by early malware such as Elk Cloner, which spread via infected boot sectors on Apple-II systems.
marking_points.quote: A program spread via boot sector infection

marking_points.point: Remote execution exploits were used for network propagation, as demonstrated by the Morris worm leveraging a debugging feature of sendmail to penetrate thousands of computers.
marking_points.quote: Used a debugging feature of sendmail (remote execution)

marking_points.point: For COM executable files, malware propagates by appending its virus body directly to the end of a legitimate host program.
marking_points.quote: Append a virus body to a program

marking_points.point: COM file infection involves replacing the original program entry point with a jump instruction that redirects execution to the virus body first.
marking_points.quote: Replace a program entry point                                   with a jump to a virus body

marking_points.point: For EXE executable files, the attack technique involves overwriting the program header so that the entry point switches to the virus code upon execution.
marking_points.quote: Over write a program header to switch the entry point to a virus

marking_points.point: Self-replication is a foundational propagation technique where programs copy themselves within shared memory environments to increase their survival chances against competing processes.
marking_points.quote: To increase their survival chances, programs can replicate themselves

questions.question: Refer to your answer in (a). Based on the scenario in (a), explain six preventive network security mechanisms that an organization can deploy to protect its infrastructure, including how each mechanism functions.

marking_points.point: A firewall is deployed to control incoming and outgoing traffic on a network by enforcing predetermined security policies.
marking_points.quote: Control incoming and outgoing traffic on network with predetermined security policies.

marking_points.point: A proxy server acts as a firewall and web filter while also caching data to speed up common requests for better network performance.
marking_points.quote: Proxy servers act as a firewall and web filter, provide shared network connections, and cache data to speed up common requests.

marking_points.point: Network segmentation establishes boundaries between network segments where computing assets share a common function, risk, or role within the organization.
marking_points.quote: Boundaries between network segments where computing assets within the segment have a common function, risk or role within an organization.

marking_points.point: A Remote Access VPN provides remote and secure access to an organization network to individual hosts or clients.
marking_points.quote: Provides remote and secure access to an organization network to individual hosts or clients

marking_points.point: Zero Trust Network Access ensures that a user should only have the access and permission required to fulfill their specific role.
marking_points.quote: A user should only has access and permission that required to fulfill the role

marking_points.point: Intrusion Detection/Prevention Systems are used to detect or prevent network security attacks such as brute force attacks, Denial-of-Service attacks, and exploits of network vulnerabilities.
marking_points.quote: To detect or prevent the network security attacks such as brute force attacks, Denial-of-Service attacks and exploits of network vulnerabilities.

questions.question: Explain six responsibilities and ethical considerations that organizations and computing professionals must address to protect privacy and uphold organizational responsibility in computer security.

marking_points.point: Information specialists have definite responsibilities in terms of performing within ethical, moral, and legal constraints when handling data.
marking_points.quote: Users in general, and information specialists in particular, have definite responsibilities in terms of performing within ethical, moral, and legal constraints

marking_points.point: Simply describing practices may not be enough when discussing the moral and ethical dimensions of ICT, requiring prescriptive organizational action.
marking_points.quote: Simply describing may not be enough when discussing the moral and ethical dimensions of ICT

marking_points.point: Organizations can adopt the Association of Computing Machinery ACM code of ethics and professional conduct to guide responsible privacy practices.
marking_points.quote: Association of Computing Machinery ACM (founded 1947) has a code of ethics and professional conduct.

marking_points.point: The Association of Information Technology Professionals provides quality IT-related education and information on relevant IT issues to support organizational responsibility.
marking_points.quote: Association of Information Technology Professionals AITP (founded 1996) – provides quality IT-related education, information on relevant IT issues, and forums for networking with experienced peers and other IT professionals.

marking_points.point: Professional bodies such as the Computer Society of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers offer established ethical standards for organizations to follow.
marking_points.quote: Computer Society of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE – CS) (founded in 1946).

marking_points.point: Organizations managing security projects can rely on the Project Management Institute, which was established in 1969, for ethical project standards.
marking_points.quote: Project Management Institute (PMI) – established in 1969.

questions.question: Describe the Samy worm as a malware case study, explaining how it exploited Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) to propagate and compromise user profiles on a social networking platform.

marking_points.point: The Samy worm injected malicious Javascript into a user profile by exploiting document.body.innerHTML.
marking_points.quote: Inject Javascript into a user proﬁle using document.body.innerHTML

marking_points.point: It retrieved the list of a user's heroes by performing a GET request on the target user's profile.
marking_points.quote: Get the list of user’s heros by using a GET on a user proﬁle

marking_points.point: The worm added its creator as a friend by executing an XML-HTTP request on the addFriends page.
marking_points.quote: Add Samy as a ﬁeld by performing XML-HTTP on the addFriends page

marking_points.point: Any visitor to an infected profile would have their own profile infected with the Javascript and their friends list modified.
marking_points.quote: Any user who visits an infected user’s page will gets proﬁle infected with Javascript and his friends list infected with Samy

marking_points.point: The attack achieved massive scale, eventually infecting approximately one million MySpace profiles.
marking_points.quote: Eventually about 1,000,000 MySpace proﬁles were infected.

marking_points.point: The underlying vulnerability exploited by such worms is that any web application returning unfiltered user input enables arbitrary script execution.
marking_points.quote: Any web application that returns user input without ﬁltering is a potential XSS vulnerability!

questions.question: Explain six characteristics of biometric mechanisms and technologies, covering their definition, categories, specific examples, and potential limitations.

marking_points.point: A biometric is defined as a physiological or behavioural characteristic that can distinguish one person from another for identification or verification purposes.
marking_points.quote: “A biometric is a physiological or behavioural characteristic of a human being that can distinguish one person from another and that theoretically can be used for identification or verification of identity.”

marking_points.point: Biometric applications are categorized into two sectors: psychological methods such as iris and fingerprint recognition, and behavioural methods such as voice and typing pattern.
marking_points.quote:
Biometric applications available today are categorized into 2 sectors
Psychological: Iris, Fingerprints, Hand, Retinal and Face recognition
Behavioural: Voice, Typing pattern, Signature

marking_points.point: Iris recognition technology scans the unique pattern of the iris, which is coloured and visible from far, requiring no physical touch.
marking_points.quote:
Scans unique pattern of iris
Iris is coloured and visible from far
No touch required

marking_points.point: Fingerprint recognition has disadvantages including susceptibility to dirt, grime, wounds, and issues with the placement of the finger during scanning.
marking_points.quote:
Dirt , grime and wounds
Placement of finger

marking_points.point: Fingerprint systems can be spoofed, making liveness detection an important requirement to ensure security.
marking_points.quote: Can be spoofed – liveness                                              important!

marking_points.point: Biometric methods serve as alternative user authentication mechanisms because passwords and shared secrets are not sufficiently secure on their own.
marking_points.quote: Alternative user authentication mechanisms are smart cards, biometric methods and two-factor authentication.
